answer: In PoA, each interaction updates an EigenTrust-style trust matrix, while temporal decay applies an exponential half-life: only sustained honest service preserves weight and influence. A freshly spawned Sybil identity has negligible incoming trust, near-zero eigenvector centrality, and no reciprocal support, so transitivity cannot elevate it into consensus. Even a river of colluding accounts remains at the nadir until independently trusted peers accumulate evidence; the garden of established identities therefore resists rapid capture.
